newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Get used to lower profits - Australia's Costello.
newsitem.headline: Get used to lower profits - Australia's Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello warned businesses to get used to lower profits as the government's policies lock in low inflation, a newspaper report said on Monday.
"I don't believe we have yet adjusted to a low inflation environment," the Australian newspaper quoted Costello as saying in an interview.
Costello said firms would have to learn that returns of two to five percent could be good results in a low-inflation environment.
Costello said this contrasted with returns like eight percent that had been easy to make in the high-inflation 1980s, the paper said.
"The big thing is educating business how to make money in a low-inflation environment," he said.
Costello said inflation was no longer a risk and the government had set Australia on course for good economic times.
"We are in an economic environment that you haven't seen since the 1980s," he said.
But he conceded Australia's high unemployment rate would not be brought down quickly.
Australia's annual consumer price index inflation was 1.3 percent in the March quarter and is forecast at 1.0 percent, year average, in the fiscal year from July 1.
The unemployment rate rose to 8.8 percent in May from 8.7 percent a month earlier.
